candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd confirms first SE1 sailings via Red Sea and Suez Canal
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd has confirmed the first westbound and eastbound sailings of the Gemini Cooperation’s SE1 service through the Red Sea and Suez Canal. The container ship Umm Qarn will operate both voyages. The announcement follows the earlier decision by Hapag-Lloyd and Maersk to transition selected Gemini services from the Cape of Good Hope route to the Red Sea and Suez Canal. According to Hapag-Lloyd, its initial transits through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait proceeded as planned and provided operational experience ahead of the SE1 passages. Each voyage will remain subject to a detailed security assessment. Transits will also take place under naval protection and in coordination with the relevant authorities and security partners. Hapag-Lloyd stressed that the move represents a gradual, service-specific approach. It does not constitute a full strategic return of the Gemini network to the Red Sea.

candidates.title: Readers Speak: Suez return advances, but normality remains distant
candidates.excerpt: Container shipping activity through the Suez Canal is increasing, but readers are not yet convinced that the route has returned to normal. Recent weeks have brought a series of moves towards the Red Sea and Suez route. Hapag-Lloyd and Maersk are returning four Gemini Cooperation services, while MSC has partially restored Suez transits on its Indusa service. Meanwhile, the OOCL Portugal recently completed a southbound Suez transit, marking COSCO Shipping Lines’ first such passage since Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb tensions disrupted shipping patterns. COSCO is now considering additional voyages through the Canal. Against that backdrop, Container News asked readers: Is Suez becoming the normal route again? The results point towards caution. Readers largely stopped short of describing the return as complete, instead favouring a more gradual or selective interpretation of the changes taking place. candidates.title: Delays mount as port disruption in Asia ties up 3m teu of box capacity
candidates.excerpt: Box shipping reliability the worst since 2022 – 'a new normal', says DP World Global container shipping reliability is at its lowest level for four years, as the congestion ... A surge in vessel delays, driven by typhoons and port disruption in Asia, has left 8.5% of the global container fleet effectively unavailable. New analysis from Sea-Intelligence suggests this equates to some 3m teu of vessel capacity – a fleet roughly equivalent in size to that of the world’s fifth-largest carrier. Schedule reliability fell to just below 50% in August, following an already sharp deterioration in July. Sea-Intelligence said reliability had fallen 12.7% over the two months, with only three periods since measurement began in 2011 recording a steeper decline. The average delay of vessels arriving late also increased, to 6.8 days, a level exceeded only during the worst disruptions of Covid. candidates.excerpt: Australian lender Metrics suspends three funds Australian alternatives manager Metrics Credit Partners has suspended trading in three of its ASX-listed funds as the country’s private credit market continues to battle headwinds. The private debt manager put two of its private credit funds, Metrics Master Income Trust and Metrics Income Opportunities Trust, into a trading halt on Monday (28 September), alongside its real estate debt and equity fund, Metrics Real Estate Multi-Strategy Fund, according to ASX filings. candidates.excerpt: THOMASTON, Conn. — A railroad museum that outgrew its space, relocated dozens of engines and cars 40 miles, and rebranded itself has put down solid roots in this northwestern Connecticut community. On Friday (Sept. 25), the 19.6-mile Naugatuck Railroad and Railroad Museum of New England jointly marked 30 years since the start of operations at Thomaston, home to 1,900 people with a legacy as a center for 19th-century clockmaking. The nonprofit museum shares shop space and a state-owned branch line with its for-profit subsidiary, the freight-hauling Naugatuck Railroad. The route was nearly abandoned after a steady erosion of freight business under New Haven, Penn Central, Conrail, Boston & Maine, and Guilford Transportation Industries. The last passenger train ran here in 1958; the last freight under prior owners in 1995. candidates.excerpt: Trains Turntable: Commentary from Association of American Railroads CEO Ian Jefferies For 10 years, See Tracks? Think Train Week has reminded Americans of a simple but essential fact: railroad tracks are not places to take chances with your safety. This annual campaign has helped raise awareness about the dangers for drivers and pedestrians around railroad tracks and crossings. But as we mark its 10th anniversary, we should also recognize that the most effective way to prevent collisions at highway-rail crossings is to eliminate the crossing altogether. That is why Congress should provide sustained, robust funding for the Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Grant Program. Every one of the nation’s 200,000 grade crossings presents a potential point of conflict between trains, vehicles, and pedestrians. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east. candidates.excerpt: VTG agrees to sell VTG Rail UK and its roughly 4,500-vehicle fleet to USS VTG has agreed to sell its UK wagon leasing business to pension scheme USS, with around 4,500 vehicles included and completion expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. The buyer is the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS), the principal pension scheme for UK universities and higher education institutions. It held around £84 billion of assets as at 31 March 2026. VTG GmbH signed a definitive sale agreement on 11 September covering all shares in VTG Rail UK Ltd. Completion is expected in the last quarter of 2026, and the companies say no regulatory approval is needed. No price has been published. VTG Rail UK within the VTG fleet VTG Rail UK has around 4,500 vehicles. The sale announcement puts the wider VTG fleet at more than 75,000 rail freight wagons, so the UK fleet represents less than 6% of that stated total.
